subject: Use when reasoning about mutation testing as a behavioral signal of test-suite quality: the mutant-operator vocabulary…

evals.prompt: Define mutation-testing in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the mutation-testing skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind mutation-testing. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "measure how much code the test suite executes (use test-coverage-strategy)". Should mutation-testing activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force mutation-testing onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to eval-driven-development, test-coverage-strategy, test-driven-development, testing-strategy.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "explain why a 90% coverage codebase might have a 40% mutation score and what that means". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying mutation-testing.

Place mutation-testing among its adjacent skills (eval-driven-development, test-coverage-strategy, test-driven-development, testing-strategy). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about mutation-testing and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
